Local

The stay, tuned to what's on.

CasaControl knows the house. Local is how it knows the place — the weather across your exact dates, what's on in town matched to who's staying, and the offers local businesses are running right now. One calendar, read two ways.

Saturday at Casa Miramar

The morning briefing · written for the surfers in your group

Surf report — 3–4 ft and clean until 11

Offshore breeze this morning; the best window is 7–10am before the tide pushes in. Full report in the guide, refreshed daily.

Surf lessons — a weekday rate, held for guests

The local surf school runs a promotion for CasaControl guests this week. The 8am slot fits the tide — say the word and it's booked.

Two beaches, two moods

Playa Azul for the lesson — five minutes, gentle break. Punta Norte for the point break — twelve minutes. Directions for both are in the guide.

Sunny, 79° by noon

The warmest day of your stay, across your exact dates. If there's a beach day in this trip, it's this one.

A morning briefing, not a guidebook

Guests don't get a binder of everything in town. They get the few right things, on the right morning — shaped by the booking itself: who's staying, what they're into, and what the weather is actually doing.

  • Matched to the group — surfers wake to the surf report and the lesson offer; families get the kid-friendly edit and the rainy-day plans. Nobody gets everything
  • Weather for the exact dates — the stay's own days, not a generic forecast, with plans that flex when it turns
  • Promotions that are current — the restaurant's Tuesday offer, the surf school's weekday rate — checked and live, never a printed list from last season
  • Where guests already are — the pre-arrival message and the guest view, opened with one tap on the block
See the guest view

October at Casa Miramar

The events calendar · read as a pricing signal

Festival weekend, Oct 23–25 — demand spikes

The food & wine festival fills the town and comparable homes are pacing well ahead. A rate lift for those nights is suggested while there's still time to price it.

Marathon Sunday — roads close early

Guests that weekend get the route map and a later-checkout suggestion in their briefing. You get the heads-up before they book, not after.

Quiet midweeks — offers do the filling

Tuesday-to-Thursday gaps are where local promotions earn their keep: the surf school's weekday rate is being shown to guests arriving on those days.

The same calendar, read the other way

For owners, Local isn't entertainment — it's foresight. The events that fill a town also move its prices, and the picks your guests see are never a black box.

  • Events as a pricing signal — festivals, marathons, holiday markets: the dates demand moves, flagged while nightly rates can still move with it
  • Full sight of the curation — exactly what your guests are being recommended, in the owner view, and a say in the picks if you'd like one
  • Kept current, continuously — events end, offers expire, forecasts change. Keeping this layer fresh is work the plan does every day, not a list someone made once
